الفصل 3: تقنيات التشفير الكلاسيكية

من قيصر إلى الوسادة لمرة واحدة: كيف يُخفى السر بمفتاح، وكيف يكسره المهاجم، وكل ما بعدها مبني على هذه الأفكار.

01 نظرة عامة

ما موضوع المحاضرة؟

المحاضرة هي الفصل الثالث من كتاب ستالينجز «Cryptography and Network Security»: تقنيات التشفير الكلاسيكية. تبدأ بتعريف المصطلحات الأساسية ونموذج التشفير المتماثل (مفتاح سري واحد للطرفين)، ثم أنواع الهجمات ومستويات الأمان، ثم تعرض عائلتين من الشيفرات: الاستبدال (قيصر، أحادية الأبجدية، بلايفير، فيجنير، الوسادة لمرة واحدة) وتبديل المواضع (سياج السكة، تبديل الصفوف).

السؤال الذي تجيب عنه: كيف نخفي رسالة بمفتاح سري، وكيف يحاول المهاجم كسرها؟ النطاق: 30 شريحة، الشيفرات الكلاسيكية فقط (DES يُذكر للمقارنة فقط).

This is Chapter 3 of Stallings, Cryptography and Network Security: Classical Encryption Techniques. It defines the core terms and the symmetric model (one secret key shared by both sides), then attack types and security levels, then two cipher families: substitution (Caesar, monoalphabetic, Playfair, Vigenère, one-time pad) and transposition (rail fence, row transposition).

The question it answers: how do we hide a message with a secret key, and how does an attacker try to break it? Scope: 30 slides, classical ciphers only (DES appears only as a comparison).

الفكرة الأساسية

أمان التشفير المتماثل يعتمد على سرية المفتاح لا سرية الخوارزمية. الشيفرة تكون ضعيفة إذا كان فضاء مفاتيحها صغيرًا (فتُكسر بالقوة الغاشمة، مثل قيصر) أو إذا تسربت إحصاءات اللغة إلى النص المشفر (فتُكسر بتحليل التكرار، مثل أحادية الأبجدية). كل شيفرة جديدة في المحاضرة تحاول سد ثغرة التي قبلها.

Symmetric security rests on the secrecy of the key, not of the algorithm. A cipher is weak if its key space is small (brute force, as with Caesar) or if language statistics leak into the ciphertext (frequency analysis, as with monoalphabetic). Each new cipher in the lecture patches the previous one's weakness.

المهارات المكتسبة

  • التمييز بين المصطلحات الأساسية وتصنيف أي شيفرة حسب الأبعاد الثلاثة.
  • تشفير وفك تشفير قيصر يدويًا بالصيغة mod 26.
  • حساب عدد المفاتيح ومتوسط محاولات القوة الغاشمة.
  • قراءة مخطط تكرار الحروف وربطه بكسر أحادية الأبجدية.
  • بناء مصفوفة بلايفير من كلمة مفتاحية.
  • تشفير رسالة بفيجنير وبسياج السكة وبتبديل الصفوف.
  • تحديد نوع الهجوم من معطيات المهاجم.
  • Distinguish the core terms and classify any cipher on the three dimensions.
  • Encrypt and decrypt Caesar by hand with mod 26.
  • Count keys and the average number of brute-force tries.
  • Read the letter-frequency chart and link it to breaking monoalphabetic ciphers.
  • Build a Playfair matrix from a keyword.
  • Encrypt with Vigenère, rail fence and row transposition.
  • Identify an attack type from what the attacker knows.

لماذا يهم؟

الشيفرات الحديثة (مثل DES وAES) مبنية على نفس فكرتي الاستبدال وتبديل المواضع، ومصممة لتسد نفس الثغرات التي تظهر هنا: فضاء مفاتيح صغير وتسرب الإحصاءات. ومفاهيم مثل أنواع الهجمات، والأمان الحسابي، وتوزيع المفاتيح تتكرر في كل الفصول التالية.

Modern ciphers (DES, AES) are built from the same two ideas, substitution and transposition, and designed to close the same gaps seen here: small key spaces and leaking statistics. Attack types, computational security and key distribution recur in every later chapter.

الشريحة 02 — Chapter 3 — Classical Encryption Techniques

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Classical Encryption Techniques

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Symmetric encryption, also referred to as conventional encryption or single-key encryption, was the only type of encryption in use prior to the development of public-key encryption in the 1970s. It remains by far the most widely used of the two types of encryption. Part One examines a number of symmetric ciphers. In this chapter, we begin with a look at a general model for the symmetric encryption process; this will enable us to understand the context within which the algorithms are used. Next, we examine a variety of algorithms in use before the computer era. Finally, we look briefly at a different approach known as steganography. Chapters 4 and 6 introduce the two most widely used symmetric cipher: DES and AES.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Chapter 3 — Classical Encryption Techniques

    الفصل الثالث موضوعه «تقنيات التشفير الكلاسيكية»: أي طرق التشفير القديمة التي سبقت الحاسوب الحديث، مثل قيصر وفيجنير والسياج.

    Chapter 3 covers classical encryption techniques: the older, pre-computer ciphers such as Caesar, Vigenère and rail fence.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

«كلاسيكية» هنا تعني أن هذه الخوارزميات تعمل على الحروف وليس على البتات، ومعظمها سهل الكسر اليوم. لكنها تعلّمنا فكرتين أساسيتين يقوم عليهما كل تشفير حديث: Substitution (الاستبدال) وTransposition (تبديل المواضع).

“Classical” means these algorithms work on letters, not bits, and most are easy to break today. They still teach the two building blocks of all modern ciphers: substitution and transposition.

الخلاصة

الفصل عن التشفير الكلاسيكي: أساس فهم التشفير الحديث.
The chapter is about classical ciphers, the foundation for modern ones.

الشريحة 03 — Definitions

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Plaintext
    • An original message
  • Ciphertext
    • The coded message
  • Enciphering/encryption
    • The process of converting from plaintext to ciphertext
  • Deciphering/decryption
    • Restoring the plaintext from the ciphertext
  • Cryptography
    • The area of study of the many schemes used for encryption
  • Cryptographic system/cipher
    • A scheme
  • Cryptanalysis
    • Techniques used for deciphering a message without any knowledge of the enciphering details
  • Cryptology
    • The areas of cryptography and cryptanalysis

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Before beginning, we define some terms. An original message is known as the plaintext, while the coded message is called the ciphertext. The process of converting from plaintext to ciphertext is known as enciphering or encryption; restoring the plaintext from the ciphertext is deciphering or decryption. The many schemes used for encryption constitute the area of study known as cryptography Such a scheme is known as a cryptographic system or a cipher. Techniques used for deciphering a message without any knowledge of the enciphering details fall into the area of cryptanalysis. Cryptanalysis is what the layperson calls “breaking the code.” The areas of cryptography and cryptanalysis together are called cryptology.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Plaintext — An original message

    النص الأصلي المقروء قبل التشفير، مثل: meet me.

    The readable original message before encryption.

  2. Ciphertext — The coded message

    الرسالة بعد التشفير، تبدو غير مفهومة، مثل: PHHW PH.

    The scrambled message after encryption.

  3. Enciphering/encryption — The process of converting from plaintext to ciphertext

    التشفير هو عملية التحويل من نص أصلي إلى نص مشفّر.

    Encryption turns plaintext into ciphertext.

  4. Deciphering/decryption — Restoring the plaintext from the ciphertext

    فك التشفير هو استرجاع النص الأصلي من النص المشفّر (بواسطة المستلم الشرعي الذي يملك المفتاح).

    Decryption restores plaintext from ciphertext (by the legitimate receiver who has the key).

  5. Cryptography — The area of study of the many schemes used for encryption

    علم التشفير: دراسة الطرق المستخدمة للتشفير.

    Cryptography is the study of encryption schemes.

  6. Cryptographic system/cipher — A scheme

    النظام التشفيري أو «الشيفرة» هو طريقة/مخطط تشفير واحد بعينه، مثل شيفرة قيصر.

    A cipher is one particular scheme, e.g. the Caesar cipher.

  7. Cryptanalysis — Techniques used for deciphering a message without any knowledge of the enciphering details

    تحليل الشيفرة: محاولة فك الرسالة دون معرفة تفاصيل التشفير (وأهمها المفتاح). هذا عمل المهاجم أو «كاسر الشيفرة».

    Cryptanalysis means breaking a message without knowing the encryption details (mainly the key): the code-breaker's job.

  8. Cryptology — The areas of cryptography and cryptanalysis

    علم التعمية يجمع المجالين معًا: التشفير + تحليل الشيفرة.

    Cryptology = cryptography + cryptanalysis.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

طريقة سهلة للتذكر:

Cryptology = Cryptography (build ciphers) + Cryptanalysis (break ciphers)
plaintext --encryption--> ciphertext --decryption--> plaintext

الفرق بين decryption وcryptanalysis مهم جدًا: الأول يقوم به المستلم الشرعي بالمفتاح، والثاني يقوم به المهاجم بدون المفتاح.

An easy way to remember it is shown above. The key distinction: decryption is done by the legitimate receiver with the key; cryptanalysis is done by an attacker without it.

تحدٍّ سريع

إذا حصل شخص على رسالة مشفّرة وحاول قراءتها دون المفتاح، هل هذا decryption أم cryptanalysis؟

الإجابة

Cryptanalysis، لأنه لا يملك تفاصيل التشفير.

Someone intercepts a ciphertext and tries to read it without the key. Is that decryption or cryptanalysis?

Answer

Cryptanalysis, because they lack the enciphering details.

الخلاصة

ثمانية مصطلحات أساسية؛ أهمها التمييز بين plaintext/ciphertext وبين decryption/cryptanalysis.
Eight core terms; above all, distinguish plaintext from ciphertext and decryption from cryptanalysis.

🖼 إظهار وصف الإتاحة

إتاحة — وصف الصورة

مخطط أفقي من اليسار إلى اليمين يتكون من خمسة عناصر متصلة بأسهم. أقصى اليسار مستطيل أخضر فاتح «كتلة بيانات (نص أصلي)». سهم عليه الحرف X يذهب إلى صندوق أخضر مستدير الزوايا «خوارزمية التشفير». سهم يخرج إلى مستطيل مخطط بنقش شبكي أسود يمثل «الكتلة المشفرة (النص المشفر)» وفوقه الصيغة Y = E(K, X). سهم آخر يذهب إلى صندوق «خوارزمية فك التشفير»، ثم سهم عليه X = D(K, Y) إلى مستطيل أخضر في أقصى اليمين «كتلة بيانات (نص أصلي)». في الأعلى رسم مفتاح مع عبارة «مفتاح سري مشترك بين المرسل والمستلم»، ومنه خط ينقسم إلى سهمين نازلين عليهما الحرف K: واحد إلى خوارزمية التشفير وواحد إلى خوارزمية فك التشفير. المعنى: نفس المفتاح يُستخدم في الطرفين.
A left-to-right diagram of five elements joined by arrows. Far left: a light-green rectangle, “Data block (plaintext)”. An arrow labelled X goes to a rounded green box, “Encryption Algorithm”. An arrow leads to a black cross-hatched rectangle, “Encrypted block (ciphertext)”, labelled above with Y = E(K, X). Another arrow goes to “Decryption Algorithm”, then an arrow labelled X = D(K, Y) leads to a green rectangle at far right, “Data block (plaintext)”. At the top, a key drawing with the text “Secret key shared by sender and recipient”; a line from it splits into two downward arrows labelled K, one into each algorithm. Meaning: the same key is used on both sides.

ترتيب القراءة

  1. ابدأ من المستطيل الأيسر: النص الأصلي X.
  2. اتبع السهم يمينًا إلى خوارزمية التشفير.
  3. اقرأ السهم النازل من الأعلى إليها: المفتاح K.
  4. تابع يمينًا إلى الكتلة المشفرة Y = E(K, X).
  5. تابع إلى خوارزمية فك التشفير، التي يصلها أيضًا المفتاح K من الأعلى.
  6. انتهِ عند المستطيل الأيمن: النص الأصلي X = D(K, Y).
  1. Start at the left rectangle: plaintext X.
  2. Follow the arrow right to the Encryption Algorithm.
  3. Read the arrow coming down into it: key K.
  4. Continue right to the encrypted block Y = E(K, X).
  5. Continue to the Decryption Algorithm, which also receives key K from above.
  6. End at the right rectangle: plaintext X = D(K, Y).

مخطط معاد بناؤه

            [ Secret key K shared by sender and recipient ]
                 |                               |
                 K                               K
                 v                               v
[Plaintext X] -> [Encryption Algorithm] -> [Ciphertext Y=E(K,X)] -> [Decryption Algorithm] -> [Plaintext X=D(K,Y)]
📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

A symmetric encryption scheme has five ingredients (Figure 3.1) ■ Plaintext: This is the original intelligible message or data that is fed into the algorithm as input. ■ Encryption algorithm: The encryption algorithm performs various substitutions and transformations on the plaintext. ■ Secret key: The secret key is also input to the encryption algorithm. The key is a value independent of the plaintext and of the algorithm. The algorithm will produce a different output depending on the specific key being used at the time. The exact substitutions and transformations performed by the algorithm depend on the key. ■ Ciphertext: This is the scrambled message produced as output. It depends on the plaintext and the secret key. For a given message, two different keys will produce two different ciphertexts. The ciphertext is an apparently random stream of data and, as it stands, is unintelligible. ■ Decryption algorithm: This is essentially the encryption algorithm run in reverse. It takes the ciphertext and the secret key and produces the original plaintext.

الصيغ

Y = E(K, X)

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: واي تساوي دالة التشفير إي للمفتاح كي والنص إكس.Y equals E of K and X: the encryption function applied to key K and plaintext X.

X = D(K, Y)

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: إكس تساوي دالة فك التشفير دي للمفتاح كي والنص المشفر واي.X equals D of K and Y: the decryption function applied to key K and ciphertext Y.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Secret key shared by sender and recipient

    المفتاح سري ويملكه الطرفان فقط؛ هذا ما يجعل التشفير «متماثلًا» (symmetric).

    Both parties hold the same secret key; that is what makes it symmetric.

  2. Y = E(K, X)

    النص المشفر Y هو ناتج تطبيق خوارزمية التشفير E على النص الأصلي X باستخدام المفتاح K.

    Ciphertext Y is the result of applying encryption E to plaintext X with key K.

  3. X = D(K, Y)

    المستلم يطبق خوارزمية فك التشفير D على Y بنفس المفتاح K فيرجع إلى X.

    The receiver applies decryption D to Y with the same key K and gets X back.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الفكرة كلها في كلمة «نفس المفتاح». الخوارزمية نفسها (E و D) ليست سرًا؛ السر الوحيد هو K. لذلك لو عرف المهاجم K انتهى الأمان، ولو لم يعرفه فلا تكفيه معرفة الخوارزمية. هذا يمهّد للشريحة التالية عن متطلبات الاستخدام الآمن.

Everything rests on “the same key”. The algorithms E and D are not secret; only K is. If an attacker learns K, security is gone; if not, knowing the algorithm is not enough. This sets up the next slide's requirements.

الخلاصة

التشفير المتماثل: مفتاح سري واحد K يستخدم للتشفير وفك التشفير.
Symmetric encryption: one secret key K for both encryption and decryption.

الشريحة 05 — Symmetric Cipher Model

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • There are two requirements for secure use of conventional encryption:
    • A strong encryption algorithm
    • Sender and receiver must have obtained copies of the secret key in a secure fashion and must keep the key secure

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

There are two requirements for secure use of conventional encryption: 1. We need a strong encryption algorithm. At a minimum, we would like the algorithm to be such that an opponent who knows the algorithm and has access to one or more ciphertexts would be unable to decipher the ciphertext or figure out the key. This requirement is usually stated in a stronger form: The opponent should be unable to decrypt ciphertext or discover the key even if he or she is in possession of a number of ciphertexts together with the plaintext that produced each ciphertext. 2. Sender and receiver must have obtained copies of the secret key in a secure fashion and must keep the key secure. If someone can discover the key and knows the algorithm, all communication using this key is readable. We assume that it is impractical to decrypt a message on the basis of the ciphertext plus knowledge of the encryption/decryption algorithm. In other words, we do not need to keep the algorithm secret; we need to keep only the key secret. This feature of symmetric encryption is what makes it feasible for widespread use. The fact that the algorithm need not be kept secret means that manufacturers can and have developed low-cost chip implementations of data encryption algorithms. These chips are widely available and incorporated into a number of products. With the use of symmetric encryption, the principal security problem is maintaining the secrecy of the key.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. There are two requirements for secure use of conventional encryption:

    لكي يكون التشفير التقليدي (المتماثل) آمنًا يجب تحقق شرطين.

    Two conditions are needed for conventional (symmetric) encryption to be secure.

  2. A strong encryption algorithm

    الشرط الأول: خوارزمية قوية، لا يستطيع المهاجم كسرها حتى لو رأى نصوصًا مشفرة كثيرة.

    First: a strong algorithm that an attacker cannot break even after seeing many ciphertexts.

  3. Sender and receiver must have obtained copies of the secret key in a secure fashion and must keep the key secure

    الشرط الثاني: يجب أن يحصل المرسل والمستلم على المفتاح بطريقة آمنة، وأن يحافظا عليه سرًا.

    Second: sender and receiver must obtain the key securely and keep it secret.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

لاحظ أن الشرطين لا يتضمنان «إخفاء الخوارزمية». أمان التشفير المتماثل يعتمد على سرية المفتاح وليس سرية الخوارزمية. الصورة الكرتونية في الشريحة (رجل يُدخل مفتاحًا في قفل) تعبير زخرفي عن هذه الفكرة.

المشكلة العملية الكبرى هي الشرط الثاني: كيف يصل المفتاح للطرف الآخر بأمان؟ ستعود هذه المشكلة في الشريحة 27 مع One-Time Pad.

Note that neither requirement says “hide the algorithm”. Security depends on the secrecy of the key, not the algorithm. The cartoon (a man inserting a key into a lock) is a decorative illustration of this.

The hard part in practice is the second requirement: getting the key to the other side safely. It returns on slide 27 with the one-time pad.

الخلاصة

شرطان: خوارزمية قوية + مفتاح يُوزَّع ويُحفظ بأمان.
Two requirements: a strong algorithm, and a key that is distributed and kept securely.

الشريحة بلا عنوان نصي؛ العنوان مأخوذ من تعليق الشكل.

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Let us take a closer look at the essential elements of a symmetric encryption scheme, using Figure 3.2.

الصيغ

X̂ , K̂

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: إكس بقبعة وكي بقبعة: تقدير المهاجم للنص الأصلي وللمفتاح.X-hat and K-hat: the attacker's estimates of the plaintext and the key.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Key Source → Secure Channel

    المفتاح يُنشأ في مكان ما ثم يُنقل إلى المستلم عبر قناة آمنة منفصلة عن قناة الرسالة.

    The key is generated somewhere and delivered to the receiver over a separate secure channel.

  2. Cryptanalyst → X̂, K̂

    المهاجم يرى النص المشفر Y فقط (لأنه على القناة العامة)، ويحاول تقدير X أو K. القبعة ^ تعني «تقدير».

    The attacker sees only Y on the public line and tries to estimate X or K; the hat ^ means “estimate”.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

هذا الشكل يكمّل الشكل 3.1 بإضافة عنصرين: من أين يأتي المفتاح (مصدر المفتاح + قناة آمنة) ومن يهاجم (محلل الشيفرة). هدف المهاجم إما استرجاع رسالة واحدة X̂ أو، وهو الأخطر، استرجاع المفتاح K̂ لأنه يفتح كل الرسائل المستقبلية.

This figure extends Figure 3.1 with two elements: where the key comes from (key source + secure channel) and who attacks (the cryptanalyst). The attacker either recovers one message X̂ or, worse, the key K̂, which unlocks all future messages.

الخلاصة

المهاجم يرى النص المشفر فقط ويحاول تقدير النص أو المفتاح؛ والمفتاح يمر بقناة آمنة.
The attacker sees only the ciphertext and tries to estimate the plaintext or key; the key travels over a secure channel.

الشريحة 07 — Cryptographic Systems

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

Characterized along three independent dimensions:

  • The type of operations used for transforming plaintext to ciphertext
    • Substitution
    • Transposition
  • The number of keys used
    • Symmetric, single-key, secret-key, conventional encryption
    • Asymmetric, two-key, or public-key encryption
  • The way in which the plaintext is processed
    • Block cipher
    • Stream cipher

[Indentation reconstructed from the slide layout; the slide file stores these lines at a single level.]

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Cryptographic systems are characterized along three independent dimensions: 1. The type of operations used for transforming plaintext to ciphertext. All encryption algorithms are based on two general principles: substitution, in which each element in the plaintext (bit, letter, group of bits or letters) is mapped into another element, and transposition, in which elements in the plaintext are rearranged. The fundamental requirement is that no information be lost (i.e., that all operations are reversible). Most systems, referred to as product systems , involve multiple stages of substitutions and transpositions. 2. The number of keys used. If both sender and receiver use the same key, the system is referred to as symmetric, single-key, secret-key, or conventional encryption. If the sender and receiver use different keys, the system is referred to as asymmetric, two-key, or public-key encryption. 3. The way in which the plaintext is processed. A block cipher processes the input one block of elements at a time, producing an output block for each input block. A stream cipher processes the input elements continuously, producing output one element at a time, as it goes along.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Characterized along three independent dimensions

    أي نظام تشفير يمكن وصفه بثلاثة أسئلة مستقلة عن بعضها.

    Any cipher can be described by three independent questions.

  2. The type of operations … Substitution / Transposition

    السؤال 1: ما نوع العملية؟ استبدال (كل حرف يُستبدل بغيره) أو تبديل مواضع (نفس الحروف لكن بترتيب مختلف).

    Q1: which operation? Substitution (each letter replaced) or transposition (same letters, rearranged).

  3. The number of keys used … Symmetric … / Asymmetric …

    السؤال 2: كم مفتاحًا؟ مفتاح واحد مشترك = متماثل (ويسمى أيضًا single-key أو secret-key أو conventional)، أو مفتاحان = غير متماثل (public-key).

    Q2: how many keys? One shared key = symmetric (also single-key, secret-key, conventional); two keys = asymmetric (public-key).

  4. The way in which the plaintext is processed … Block cipher / Stream cipher

    السؤال 3: كيف يُعالَج النص؟ على شكل كتل ثابتة الحجم (block) أو تدفق عنصرًا بعد عنصر (stream).

    Q3: how is the plaintext processed? In fixed-size blocks, or as a stream one element at a time.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

«مستقلة» تعني أن أي اختيار في بُعد لا يفرض شيئًا في البُعدين الآخرين. مثال من هذه المحاضرة: شيفرة قيصر = استبدال + متماثلة + تعالج حرفًا بحرف. وشيفرة السياج Rail Fence = تبديل مواضع + متماثلة.

“Independent” means a choice on one axis says nothing about the others. From this lecture: Caesar = substitution + symmetric + letter by letter; Rail Fence = transposition + symmetric.

الخلاصة

ثلاثة أبعاد: نوع العملية (استبدال/تبديل)، عدد المفاتيح (1/2)، طريقة المعالجة (كتلة/تدفق).
Three dimensions: operation (substitution/transposition), number of keys (1/2), processing (block/stream).

الشريحة 08 — Cryptanalysis and Brute-Force Attack

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Cryptanalysis
    • Attack relies on the nature of the algorithm plus some knowledge of the general characteristics of the plaintext
    • Attack exploits the characteristics of the algorithm to attempt to deduce a specific plaintext or to deduce the key being used
  • Brute-force attack
    • Attacker tries every possible key on a piece of ciphertext until an intelligible translation into plaintext is obtained
    • On average, half of all possible keys must be tried to achieve success

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Typically, the objective of attacking an encryption system is to recover the key in use rather than simply to recover the plaintext of a single ciphertext. There are two general approaches to attacking a conventional encryption scheme: • Cryptanalysis: Cryptanalytic attacks rely on the nature of the algorithm plus perhaps some knowledge of the general characteristics of the plaintext or even some sample plaintext–ciphertext pairs. This type of attack exploits the characteristics of the algorithm to attempt to deduce a specific plaintext or to deduce the key being used. • Brute-force attack: The attacker tries every possible key on a piece of ciphertext until an intelligible translation into plaintext is obtained. On average, half of all possible keys must be tried to achieve success. If either type of attack succeeds in deducing the key, the effect is catastrophic: All future and past messages encrypted with that key are compromised.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Cryptanalysis — Attack relies on the nature of the algorithm plus some knowledge of the general characteristics of the plaintext

    تحليل الشيفرة يعتمد على فهم طبيعة الخوارزمية، مع معرفة عامة بشكل النص الأصلي (مثلًا أنه نص إنجليزي).

    Cryptanalysis uses how the algorithm works plus general knowledge of the plaintext (e.g. that it is English).

  2. Attack exploits the characteristics of the algorithm to attempt to deduce a specific plaintext or to deduce the key being used

    الهدف إما استنتاج نص أصلي معيّن أو استنتاج المفتاح نفسه.

    The goal is to deduce a particular plaintext or the key itself.

  3. Brute-force attack — Attacker tries every possible key on a piece of ciphertext until an intelligible translation into plaintext is obtained

    هجوم القوة الغاشمة: تجربة كل المفاتيح الممكنة واحدًا تلو الآخر حتى يظهر نص مفهوم.

    Brute force: try every possible key until readable text appears.

  4. On average, half of all possible keys must be tried to achieve success

    في المتوسط نحتاج تجربة نصف المفاتيح قبل إيجاد الصحيح.

    On average you must try half of all keys.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الفرق الجوهري: تحليل الشيفرة ذكي يستغل نقاط ضعف الخوارزمية، والقوة الغاشمة أعمى لا يحتاج أي ضعف لكنه بطيء ويعتمد على حجم فضاء المفاتيح.

لماذا «النصف»؟ المفتاح الصحيح يمكن أن يكون في أي موضع من القائمة بنفس الاحتمال، فمتوسط موقعه هو منتصفها.

The essential difference: cryptanalysis is clever and exploits weaknesses; brute force is blind, needs no weakness, but is slow and depends on key-space size.

Why half? The right key is equally likely to be anywhere in the list, so on average it sits in the middle.

مثال رقمي محلول

إذا كان عدد المفاتيح الممكنة 1000، فالمتوسط ≈ 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 محاولة. ولو كانت 25 (قيصر) فالمتوسط ≈ 12.5 محاولة.

With 1000 possible keys, the average is about 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 tries. With 25 keys (Caesar), about 12.5 tries.

الخلاصة

تحليل الشيفرة يستغل خصائص الخوارزمية؛ القوة الغاشمة تجرب كل المفاتيح (المتوسط: النصف).
Cryptanalysis exploits the algorithm; brute force tries every key (half on average).

إتاحة — وصف الصورة

صورة جدول بعمودين وخمسة صفوف، الخلايا رمادية فاتحة بحدود سوداء. العمود الأيسر «نوع الهجوم» والأيمن «ما يعرفه محلل الشيفرة» كقوائم نقطية. كل صف يضيف معلومات على الصف الذي قبله تقريبًا: البندان الأولان (خوارزمية التشفير، النص المشفر) مكرران في كل الصفوف.
An image of a two-column, five-row table with light-grey cells and black borders. Left column “Type of Attack”, right column “Known to Cryptanalyst” as bullet lists. Each row roughly adds information to the previous one; the first two bullets (encryption algorithm, ciphertext) repeat in every row.

ترتيب القراءة

  1. اقرأ عناوين الأعمدة.
  2. ثم كل صف من الأعلى للأسفل: اسم الهجوم ثم قائمته النقطية.
  1. Read the column headers.
  2. Then each row top to bottom: attack name, then its bullet list.
📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Table 3.1 summarizes the various types of cryptanalytic attacks based on the amount of information known to the cryptanalyst. The most difficult problem is presented when all that is available is the ciphertext only . In some cases, not even the encryption algorithm is known, but in general, we can assume that the opponent does know the algorithm used for encryption. One possible attack under these circumstances is the brute-force approach of trying all possible keys. If the key space is very large, this becomes impractical. Thus, the opponent must rely on an analysis of the ciphertext itself, generally applying various statistical tests to it. To use this approach, the opponent must have some general idea of the type of plaintext that is concealed, such as English or French text, an EXE file, a Java source listing, an accounting file, and so on. The ciphertext-only attack is the easiest to defend against because the opponent has the least amount of information to work with. In many cases, however, the analyst has more information. The analyst may be able to capture one or more plaintext messages as well as their encryptions. Or the analyst may know that certain plaintext patterns will appear in a message. For example, a file that is encoded in the Postscript format always begins with the same pattern, or there may be a standardized header or banner to an electronic funds transfer message, and so on. All these are examples of known plaintext . With this knowledge, the analyst may be able to deduce the key on the basis of the way in which the known plaintext is transformed. Closely related to the known-plaintext attack is what might be referred to as a probable-word attack. If the opponent is working with the encryption of some general prose message, he or she may have little knowledge of what is in the message. However, if the opponent is after some very specific information, then parts of the message may be known. For example, if an entire accounting file is being transmitted, the opponent may know the placement of certain key words in the header of the file. As another example, the source code for a program developed by Corporation X might include a copyright statement in some standardized position. If the analyst is able somehow to get the source system to insert into the system a message chosen by the analyst, then a chosen-plaintext attack is possible. In general, if the analyst is able to choose the messages to encrypt, the analyst may deliberately pick patterns that can be expected to reveal the structure of the key. Table 3.1 lists two other types of attack: chosen ciphertext and chosen text. These are less commonly employed as cryptanalytic techniques but are nevertheless possible avenues of attack.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Ciphertext Only

    أضعف موقف للمهاجم: يعرف الخوارزمية والنص المشفر فقط.

    Weakest attacker position: knows only the algorithm and the ciphertext.

  2. Known Plaintext

    يعرف أيضًا أزواجًا من (نص أصلي، نص مشفر) بنفس المفتاح، مثل ترويسة رسالة معروفة.

    Also knows some (plaintext, ciphertext) pairs under the same key, e.g. a known message header.

  3. Chosen Plaintext

    يستطيع اختيار نص أصلي ويحصل على تشفيره.

    Can choose a plaintext and get its encryption.

  4. Chosen Ciphertext

    يستطيع اختيار نص مشفر ويحصل على فك تشفيره.

    Can choose a ciphertext and get its decryption.

  5. Chosen Text

    يجمع القدرتين: اختيار نص أصلي واختيار نص مشفر.

    Combines both: chosen plaintext and chosen ciphertext.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

رتّب الهجمات حسب قوة المهاجم، من الأقل معرفة إلى الأكثر: Ciphertext Only ← Known Plaintext ← Chosen Plaintext / Chosen Ciphertext ← Chosen Text. كلما زادت معرفة المهاجم صار الكسر أسهل، لذلك الخوارزمية الجيدة يجب أن تصمد حتى أمام المهاجم الأقوى.

الفرق بين «Known» و«Chosen»: في Known المهاجم يصادف أزواجًا موجودة، أما في Chosen فيختار هو ما يريد تشفيره.

Order the attacks by attacker power, least to most knowledge: Ciphertext Only → Known Plaintext → Chosen Plaintext / Chosen Ciphertext → Chosen Text. More knowledge makes breaking easier, so a good algorithm must survive the strongest attacker.

Known vs Chosen: with “known”, the attacker happens to have pairs; with “chosen”, the attacker picks what gets encrypted.

الخلاصة

خمسة أنواع هجمات تختلف بما يعرفه المهاجم؛ Ciphertext Only هو الأصعب للمهاجم.
Five attack types differ by what the attacker knows; ciphertext-only is the hardest for the attacker.

الشريحة 10 — Encryption Scheme Security

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Unconditionally secure
    • No matter how much time an opponent has, it is impossible for him or her to decrypt the ciphertext simply because the required information is not there
  • Computationally secure
    • The cost of breaking the cipher exceeds the value of the encrypted information
    • The time required to break the cipher exceeds the useful lifetime of the information

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Two more definitions are worthy of note. An encryption scheme is unconditionally secure if the ciphertext generated by the scheme does not contain enough information to determine uniquely the corresponding plaintext, no matter how much ciphertext is available. That is, no matter how much time an opponent has, it is impossible for him or her to decrypt the ciphertext simply because the required information is not there. With the exception of a scheme known as the one-time pad (described later in this chapter), there is no encryption algorithm that is unconditionally secure. Therefore, all that the users of an encryption algorithm can strive for is an algorithm that meets one or both of the following criteria: • The cost of breaking the cipher exceeds the value of the encrypted information. • The time required to break the cipher exceeds the useful lifetime of the information. An encryption scheme is said to be computationally secure if either of the foregoing two criteria are met. Unfortunately, it is very difficult to estimate the amount of effort required to cryptanalyze ciphertext successfully. All forms of cryptanalysis for symmetric encryption schemes are designed to exploit the fact that traces of structure or pattern in the plaintext may survive encryption and be discernible in the ciphertext. This will become clear as we examine various symmetric encryption schemes in this chapter. We will see in Part Three that cryptanalysis for public-key schemes proceeds from a fundamentally different premise, namely, that the mathematical properties of the pair of keys may make it possible for one of the two keys to be deduced from the other.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Unconditionally secure — No matter how much time an opponent has, it is impossible for him or her to decrypt the ciphertext simply because the required information is not there

    آمن بلا شروط: مهما امتلك المهاجم من وقت (وقدرة حاسوبية) لا يمكنه فك الشيفرة، لأن المعلومة المطلوبة غير موجودة أصلًا في النص المشفر.

    Unconditionally secure: no amount of time lets the opponent decrypt, because the needed information simply isn't in the ciphertext.

  2. Computationally secure — The cost of breaking the cipher exceeds the value of the encrypted information

    آمن حسابيًا (الشرط 1): تكلفة الكسر أكبر من قيمة المعلومة نفسها.

    Computationally secure (condition 1): breaking costs more than the information is worth.

  3. The time required to break the cipher exceeds the useful lifetime of the information

    الشرط 2: الوقت اللازم للكسر أطول من عمر فائدة المعلومة.

    Condition 2: breaking takes longer than the information stays useful.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

«آمن بلا شروط» مستوى نظري مثالي؛ في هذه المحاضرة المثال الوحيد عليه هو One-Time Pad (الشريحة 26–27). أما معظم الأنظمة العملية فهي «آمنة حسابيًا»: يمكن كسرها نظريًا، لكن ليس بتكلفة أو وقت معقولين.

مثال: خطة عسكرية تفقد قيمتها بعد أسبوع؛ إذا كان كسرها يحتاج سنة فهي آمنة حسابيًا. الصورة في الشريحة (خزنة مفتوحة فيها حاسوب وأرقام ثنائية) زخرفية.

Unconditional security is an ideal; in this lecture the only example is the one-time pad (slides 26–27). Most practical systems are computationally secure: breakable in theory, but not at reasonable cost or time.

Example: a military plan useless after a week is computationally secure if breaking it takes a year. The slide image (an open safe holding a computer and binary digits) is decorative.

الخلاصة

بلا شروط = مستحيل الكسر؛ حسابيًا = الكسر أغلى أو أبطأ من قيمة المعلومة.
Unconditional = impossible to break; computational = breaking costs more or takes longer than the information is worth.

الشريحة 11 — Brute-Force Attack

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Involves trying every possible key until an intelligible translation of the ciphertext into plaintext is obtained
  • On average, half of all possible keys must be tried to achieve success
  • To supplement the brute-force approach, some degree of knowledge about the expected plaintext is needed, and some means of automatically distinguishing plaintext from garble is also needed

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

A brute-force attack involves trying every possible key until an intelligible translation of the ciphertext into plaintext is obtained. On average, half of all possible keys must be tried to achieve success. That is, if there are X different keys, on average an attacker would discover the actual key after X/2 tries. It is important to note that there is more to a brute-force attack than simply running through all possible keys. Unless known plaintext is provided, the analyst must be able to recognize plaintext as plaintext. If the message is just plain text in English, then the result pops out easily, although the task of recognizing English would have to be automated. If the text message has been compressed before encryption, then recognition is more difficult. And if the message is some more general type of data, such as a numerical file, and this has been compressed, the problem becomes even more difficult to automate. Thus, to supplement the brute-force approach, some degree of knowledge about the expected plaintext is needed, and some means of automatically distinguishing plaintext from garble is also needed.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Involves trying every possible key until an intelligible translation of the ciphertext into plaintext is obtained

    القوة الغاشمة = تجربة كل مفتاح ممكن حتى يظهر نص مفهوم.

    Brute force = try every possible key until intelligible plaintext appears.

  2. On average, half of all possible keys must be tried to achieve success

    المتوسط: نصف المفاتيح (تكرار لما في الشريحة 8 للتأكيد).

    On average, half the keys (repeated from slide 8 for emphasis).

  3. To supplement the brute-force approach, some degree of knowledge about the expected plaintext is needed, and some means of automatically distinguishing plaintext from garble is also needed

    لكن القوة الغاشمة وحدها لا تكفي: يجب أن نعرف شيئًا عن شكل النص المتوقع، وأن نملك طريقة آلية للتمييز بين النص الحقيقي والكلام العشوائي (garble).

    Brute force alone is not enough: you need some knowledge of what the plaintext looks like and an automatic way to tell real text from garble.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

تخيّل أنك جربت مفتاحًا فظهرت لك سلسلة حروف؛ كيف يعرف الحاسوب أنها الرسالة الصحيحة؟ إذا كانت الرسالة إنجليزية فسيتعرف عليها بسهولة. لكن إذا كانت مضغوطة (كما في الشكل 3.4، الشريحة 17) فستبدو عشوائية حتى بعد فكّها الصحيح، فيصعب التمييز.

Imagine trying a key and getting a string of letters: how does a computer know it is the right message? English plaintext is easy to recognise. But compressed data (Figure 3.4, slide 17) looks random even when correctly decrypted, so recognition becomes hard.

الخلاصة

القوة الغاشمة تحتاج معرفة بالنص المتوقع وطريقة لتمييزه عن العشوائي.
Brute force needs knowledge of the expected plaintext and a way to tell it from garble.

الشريحة 12 — Strong Encryption

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • The term strong encryption refers to encryption schemes that make it impractically difficult for unauthorized persons or systems to gain access to plaintext that has been encrypted
  • Properties that make an encryption algorithm strong are:
    • Appropriate choice of cryptographic algorithm
      • Use of sufficiently long key lengths
      • Appropriate choice of protocols
      • A well-engineered implementation
      • Absence of deliberately introduced hidden flaws

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

For users, security managers, and organization executives, there is a requirement for strong encryption to protect data. The term strong encryption is an imprecise one, but in general terms, it refers to encryption schemes that make it impractically difficult for unauthorized persons or systems to gain access to plaintext that has been encrypted. [NAS18] lists the following properties that make an encryption algorithm strong: appropriate choice of cryptographic algorithm, use of sufficiently long key lengths, appropriate choice of protocols, a well-engineered implementation, and the absence of deliberately introduced hidden flaws. The first two factors relate to cryptanalysis, discussed in this section, and the third factor relates to the discussion in Part Six. The last two factors are beyond the scope of this book.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. The term strong encryption refers to encryption schemes that make it impractically difficult for unauthorized persons or systems to gain access to plaintext that has been encrypted

    «التشفير القوي» هو الذي يجعل الوصول للنص الأصلي صعبًا لدرجة غير عملية على غير المصرح لهم.

    “Strong encryption” makes it impractically hard for unauthorized parties to reach the plaintext.

  2. Appropriate choice of cryptographic algorithm

    اختيار خوارزمية مناسبة.

    Choose a suitable algorithm.

  3. Use of sufficiently long key lengths

    مفاتيح طويلة بما يكفي (لمقاومة القوة الغاشمة).

    Keys long enough (to resist brute force).

  4. Appropriate choice of protocols

    اختيار بروتوكولات مناسبة لاستخدام الخوارزمية.

    Use suitable protocols around the algorithm.

  5. A well-engineered implementation

    تنفيذ برمجي متقن بلا أخطاء.

    A well-engineered implementation.

  6. Absence of deliberately introduced hidden flaws

    عدم وجود ثغرات خفية مزروعة عمدًا (أبواب خلفية).

    No deliberately hidden flaws (backdoors).

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الرسالة الأساسية: قوة التشفير ليست في الخوارزمية وحدها. خوارزمية ممتازة بمفتاح قصير، أو بتنفيذ فيه خطأ، أو ببروتوكول ضعيف، أو بباب خلفي مقصود، تصبح ضعيفة. فكّر فيها كسلسلة: قوتها بقوة أضعف حلقة.

The core message: strength is not in the algorithm alone. An excellent algorithm with a short key, a buggy implementation, a weak protocol, or a deliberate backdoor becomes weak. Think of a chain: as strong as its weakest link.

الخلاصة

خمس خصائص للتشفير القوي: خوارزمية، طول مفتاح، بروتوكولات، تنفيذ متقن، بلا ثغرات مقصودة.
Five properties of strong encryption: algorithm, key length, protocols, sound implementation, no hidden flaws.

الشريحة 13 — Substitution Technique

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Is one in which the letters of plaintext are replaced by other letters or by numbers or symbols
  • If the plaintext is viewed as a sequence of bits, then substitution involves replacing plaintext bit patterns with ciphertext bit patterns

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

The two basic building blocks of all encryption techniques are substitution and transposition. We examine these in the next two sections. Finally, we discuss a system that combines both substitution and transposition. A substitution technique is one in which the letters of plaintext are replaced by other letters or by numbers or symbols. If the plaintext is viewed as a sequence of bits, then substitution involves replacing plaintext bit patterns with ciphertext bit patterns.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Is one in which the letters of plaintext are replaced by other letters or by numbers or symbols

    تقنية الاستبدال: كل حرف في النص الأصلي يُستبدل بحرف آخر أو رقم أو رمز.

    Substitution: each plaintext letter is replaced by another letter, number or symbol.

  2. If the plaintext is viewed as a sequence of bits, then substitution involves replacing plaintext bit patterns with ciphertext bit patterns

    إذا نظرنا للنص كسلسلة بتات (كما في الحاسوب)، فالاستبدال يعني استبدال أنماط بتات بأنماط أخرى.

    If the plaintext is bits, substitution replaces plaintext bit patterns with ciphertext bit patterns.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

هذه الشريحة تفتتح العائلة الأولى من الشيفرات: قيصر، أحادية الأبجدية، بلايفير، متعددة الأبجدية (فيجنير)، والوسادة لمرة واحدة. كلها تغيّر هوية الحروف. لاحقًا (الشريحة 28) تبدأ عائلة Transposition التي تغيّر مواضعها فقط. الصورة الصغيرة (يد تقلّب كتابًا بحروف ملوّنة) زخرفية.

This slide opens the first family of ciphers: Caesar, monoalphabetic, Playfair, polyalphabetic (Vigenère) and one-time pad. All of them change the letters' identity. Later (slide 28) the transposition family changes only their positions. The small image (a hand flipping a book of coloured letters) is decorative.

الخلاصة

الاستبدال = تغيير الحروف (أو أنماط البتات) بغيرها.
Substitution = replacing letters (or bit patterns) with others.

الشريحة 14 — Caesar Cipher

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Simplest and earliest known use of a substitution cipher
  • Used by Julius Caesar
  • Involves replacing each letter of the alphabet with the letter standing three places further down the alphabet
  • Alphabet is wrapped around so that the letter following Z is A
plain:    meet    me    after    the    toga    party
cipher:   PHHW    PH    DIWHU    WKH    WRJD    SDUWB

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

The earliest known, and the simplest, use of a substitution cipher was by Julius Caesar. The Caesar cipher involves replacing each letter of the alphabet with the letter standing three places further down the alphabet.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Simplest and earliest known use of a substitution cipher

    أبسط وأقدم شيفرة استبدال معروفة.

    The simplest and earliest known substitution cipher.

  2. Used by Julius Caesar

    استخدمها يوليوس قيصر (لذلك سميت باسمه؛ الصورة في الشريحة رسم زخرفي لروما وتمثال قيصر).

    Used by Julius Caesar (hence the name; the slide image is a decorative drawing of Rome and a Caesar statue).

  3. Involves replacing each letter of the alphabet with the letter standing three places further down the alphabet

    كل حرف يُستبدل بالحرف الذي يليه بثلاثة مواضع: a ← D، b ← E، …

    Each letter is replaced by the one three places later: a → D, b → E, …

  4. Alphabet is wrapped around so that the letter following Z is A

    الأبجدية دائرية: بعد z نعود إلى a، فيصبح x ← A، y ← B، z ← C.

    The alphabet wraps: after z comes a, so x → A, y → B, z → C.

  5. plain: meet me after the toga party / cipher: PHHW PH DIWHU WKH WRJD SDUWB

    مثال كامل: كل حرف أُزيح 3 مواضع.

    Full example: every letter shifted by 3.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

لاحظ الاصطلاح في الكتاب: النص الأصلي بأحرف صغيرة والنص المشفر بأحرف كبيرة. وتلاحظ أيضًا أن المسافات تُركت كما هي في المثال لتسهيل القراءة.

Note the book's convention: plaintext in lowercase, ciphertext in UPPERCASE. The spaces are kept in the example only for readability.

مثال رقمي محلول

تحقق من أول كلمة: m ← P، e ← H، e ← H، t ← W، إذن meet ← PHHW. وparty: p←S، a←D، r←U، t←W، y←B (التفاف: y + 3 يتجاوز z فيرجع إلى B).

Check the first word: m → P, e → H, e → H, t → W, so meet → PHHW. And party: p→S, a→D, r→U, t→W, y→B (wrap-around: y + 3 passes z and lands on B).

الخلاصة

قيصر: إزاحة كل حرف 3 مواضع مع الالتفاف بعد Z.
Caesar: shift each letter 3 places, wrapping after Z.

الشريحة 15 — Caesar Cipher Algorithm

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

Can define transformation as:

Caesar transformation (shift 3)
plainabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
cipherDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZABC

Mathematically give each letter a number

Letter numbering
letterabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
number012345678910111213141516171819202122232425

Algorithm can be expressed as:

c = E(3, p) = (p + 3) mod (26)

A shift may be of any amount, so that the general Caesar algorithm is:

C =  E(k , p ) =  (p + k ) mod 26

Where k takes on a value in the range 1 to 25; the decryption algorithm is simply:

p =  D(k , C ) =  (C - k ) mod 26

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Note that the alphabet is wrapped around, so that the letter following Z is A. An algorithm can be expressed as follows. For each plaintext letter p , substitute the ciphertext letter C

الصيغ

c = E(3, p) = (p + 3) mod 26

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: سي تساوي إي لثلاثة وبي، وتساوي بي زائد ثلاثة، باقي القسمة على ستة وعشرين.c equals E of 3 and p, which equals p plus three, mod twenty-six.

C = E(k, p) = (p + k) mod 26

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: سي الكبيرة تساوي إي لكي وبي، وتساوي بي زائد كي، باقي القسمة على ستة وعشرين.Capital C equals E of k and p, which equals p plus k, mod twenty-six.

p = D(k, C) = (C - k) mod 26

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: بي تساوي دي لكي وسي، وتساوي سي ناقص كي، باقي القسمة على ستة وعشرين.p equals D of k and C, which equals C minus k, mod twenty-six.

1 <= k <= 25

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: كي أكبر من أو يساوي واحد، وأصغر من أو يساوي خمسة وعشرين.k is greater than or equal to one and less than or equal to twenty-five.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Can define transformation as: a b c … → D E F …

    يمكن كتابة التحويل كجدول: كل حرف أصلي وتحته الحرف المشفر.

    The transformation can be written as a two-row table: each plain letter above its cipher letter.

  2. Mathematically give each letter a number (a=0 … z=25)

    نعطي كل حرف رقمًا: a=0، b=1، … z=25، لكي نحسب بالرياضيات.

    Number the letters a=0 … z=25 so we can compute.

  3. c = E(3, p) = (p + 3) mod (26)

    التشفير: نجمع 3 ثم نأخذ باقي القسمة على 26 (هذا ما يحقق الالتفاف).

    Encryption: add 3, then take the remainder mod 26 (this gives the wrap-around).

  4. C = E(k, p) = (p + k) mod 26

    الصيغة العامة: الإزاحة k يمكن أن تكون أي قيمة، وليس 3 فقط.

    General form: the shift k can be any amount, not only 3.

  5. Where k takes on a value in the range 1 to 25

    المفتاح k بين 1 و 25 فقط، أي 25 مفتاحًا ممكنًا (الإزاحة 0 لا تغيّر شيئًا).

    k ranges from 1 to 25, i.e. 25 possible keys (a shift of 0 changes nothing).

  6. p = D(k, C) = (C - k) mod 26

    فك التشفير: نطرح k ثم نأخذ باقي القسمة على 26.

    Decryption: subtract k, then take mod 26.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

mod 26 هو «باقي القسمة على 26»، وهو ما يجعل الأبجدية دائرية: إذا تجاوز الناتج 25 نرجع للبداية، وإذا صار سالبًا عند فك التشفير نضيف 26.

mod 26 is the remainder after dividing by 26; it makes the alphabet circular. Past 25 we wrap to the start, and a negative result during decryption has 26 added.

مثال رقمي محلول

تشفير y بالمفتاح 3: y = 24 ← (24 + 3) mod 26 = 27 mod 26 = 1 ← B.

فك تشفير A بالمفتاح 3: A = 0 ← (0 − 3) mod 26 = −3 + 26 = 23 ← x.

تشفير t بالمفتاح 10: t = 19 ← 29 mod 26 = 3 ← D.

Encrypt y with k=3: y = 24 → (24 + 3) mod 26 = 27 mod 26 = 1 → B.

Decrypt A with k=3: A = 0 → (0 − 3) mod 26 = −3 + 26 = 23 → x.

Encrypt t with k=10: t = 19 → 29 mod 26 = 3 → D.

تحدٍّ سريع

ما ناتج تشفير الحرف z بالمفتاح 1؟

الإجابة

(25 + 1) mod 26 = 0 ← A.

What does z encrypt to with k = 1?

Answer

(25 + 1) mod 26 = 0 → A.

الخلاصة

قيصر رياضيًا: C = (p + k) mod 26، p = (C − k) mod 26، و k من 1 إلى 25.
Caesar mathematically: C = (p + k) mod 26, p = (C − k) mod 26, with k from 1 to 25.

If it is known that a given ciphertext is a Caesar cipher, then a brute-force cryptanalysis is easily performed: simply try all the 25 possible keys. Figure 3.3 shows the results of applying this strategy to the example ciphertext. In this case, the plaintext leaps out as occupying the third line. Three important characteristics of this problem enabled us to use a brute-force cryptanalysis: 1. The encryption and decryption algorithms are known. 2. There are only 25 keys to try. 3. The language of the plaintext is known and easily recognizable.

Why does brute force work against Caesar? The slide notes give three reasons: (1) the encryption and decryption algorithms are known, (2) there are only 25 keys, (3) the plaintext language is known and easy to recognise. Change any of these (a huge key space, or hard-to-recognise plaintext) and brute force gets much harder.

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

In most networking situations, we can assume that the algorithms are known. What generally makes brute-force cryptanalysis impractical is the use of an algorithm that employs a large number of keys. For example, the triple DES algorithm, examined in Chapter 7, makes use of a 168-bit key, giving a key space of 2168 or greater than 3.7 * 1050 possible keys. The third characteristic is also significant. If the language of the plaintext is unknown, then plaintext output may not be recognizable. Furthermore, the input may be abbreviated or compressed in some fashion, again making recognition difficult. For example, Figure 3.4 shows a portion of a text file compressed using an algorithm called ZIP. If this file is then encrypted with a simple substitution cipher (expanded to include more than just 26 alphabetic characters), then the plaintext may not be recognized when it is uncovered in the brute-force cryptanalysis.

الشريحة 18 — Monoalphabetic Cipher

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Permutation
    • Of a finite set of elements S is an ordered sequence of all the elements of S , with each element appearing exactly once
    • If the “cipher” line can be any permutation of the 26 alphabetic characters, then there are 26! or greater than 4 x 1026 possible keys
    • This is 10 orders of magnitude greater than the key space for DES
    • Approach is referred to as a monoalphabetic substitution cipher because a single cipher alphabet is used per message

[The exponent “26” in 1026 is a superscript on the slide; plain text extraction shows it as “1026”.]

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

With only 25 possible keys, the Caesar cipher is far from secure. A dramatic increase in the key space can be achieved by allowing an arbitrary substitution. Before proceeding, we define the term permutation . A permutation of a finite set of elements S is an ordered sequence of all the elements of S, with each element appearing exactly once. For example, if S = {a, b, c}, there are six permutations of S : abc, acb, bac, bca, cab, cba In general, there are n ! permutations of a set of n elements, because the first element can be chosen in one of n ways, the second in n - 1 ways, the third in n - 2 ways, and so on. If, instead, the “cipher” line can be any permutation of the 26 alphabetic characters, then there are 26! or greater than 4 * 1026 possible keys. This is 10 orders of magnitude greater than the key space for DES and would seem to eliminate brute-force techniques for cryptanalysis. Such an approach is referred to as a monoalphabetic substitution cipher, because a single cipher alphabet (mapping from plain alphabet to cipher alphabet) is used per message.

الصيغ

26! > 4 x 10^26

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: مضروب ستة وعشرين أكبر من أربعة في عشرة أس ستة وعشرين.Twenty-six factorial is greater than four times ten to the power of twenty-six.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Permutation of a finite set of elements S is an ordered sequence of all the elements of S, with each element appearing exactly once

    التبديلة (permutation): ترتيب لكل عناصر المجموعة، وكل عنصر يظهر مرة واحدة فقط.

    A permutation is an ordering of all elements of a set, each appearing exactly once.

  2. If the “cipher” line can be any permutation of the 26 alphabetic characters, then there are 26! or greater than 4 x 10^26 possible keys

    بدل الإزاحة الثابتة، يمكن أن يكون سطر الشيفرة أي ترتيب للحروف الـ 26، فيصبح عدد المفاتيح 26! (أكثر من 4 × 10^26).

    Instead of a fixed shift, the cipher line can be any ordering of the 26 letters, giving 26! keys (more than 4 × 10^26).

  3. This is 10 orders of magnitude greater than the key space for DES

    هذا أكبر من فضاء مفاتيح DES بحوالي 10 مراتب عشرية (أي 10^10 مرة).

    That is about 10 orders of magnitude (10^10 times) larger than DES's key space.

  4. Approach is referred to as a monoalphabetic substitution cipher because a single cipher alphabet is used per message

    سميت «أحادية الأبجدية» لأن الرسالة كلها تستخدم أبجدية شيفرة واحدة ثابتة.

    Called monoalphabetic because one fixed cipher alphabet is used for the whole message.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

المقارنة مع قيصر: قيصر = 25 مفتاحًا فقط، أما أحادية الأبجدية = 26! مفتاحًا، فلا يمكن كسرها بالقوة الغاشمة. لكن هذا لا يعني أنها آمنة: الشريحتان 19–20 تبيّنان أنها تُكسر بتحليل تكرار الحروف.

Compared with Caesar: Caesar has just 25 keys; monoalphabetic has 26!, far beyond brute force. That does not make it secure: slides 19–20 show it falls to letter-frequency analysis.

مثال رقمي محلول

26! = 403,291,461,126,605,635,584,000,000 ≈ 4.03 × 10^26.
مفتاح DES طوله 56 بت، إذن 2^56 ≈ 7.2 × 10^16 مفتاح.
النسبة: 4 × 10^26 ÷ 7.2 × 10^16 ≈ 5.6 × 10^9 ≈ 10^10، وهذا معنى «10 مراتب».

26! = 403,291,461,126,605,635,584,000,000 ≈ 4.03 × 10^26.
DES uses a 56-bit key, so 2^56 ≈ 7.2 × 10^16 keys.
Ratio: 4 × 10^26 ÷ 7.2 × 10^16 ≈ 5.6 × 10^9 ≈ 10^10, which is what “10 orders of magnitude” means.

الخلاصة

أحادية الأبجدية: أي تبديلة للحروف = 26! مفتاحًا، أبجدية واحدة لكل الرسالة.
Monoalphabetic: any permutation of the letters = 26! keys, one alphabet per message.

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

There is, however, another line of attack. If the cryptanalyst knows the nature of the plaintext (e.g., noncompressed English text), then the analyst can exploit the regularities of the language. To see how such a cryptanalysis might proceed, we give a partial example here that is adapted from one in [SINK09]. The ciphertext to be solved is UZQSOVUOHXMOPVGPOZPEVSGZWSZOPFPESXUDBMETSXAIZ VUEPHZHMDZSHZOWSFPAPPDTSVPQUZWYMXUZUHSX EPYEPOPDZSZUFPOMBZWPFUPZHMDJUDTMOHMQ As a first step, the relative frequency of the letters can be determined and compared to a standard frequency distribution for English, such as is shown in Figure 3.5 (based on [LEWA00]). If the message were long enough, this technique alone might be sufficient, but because this is a relatively short message, we cannot expect an exact match. In any case, the relative frequencies of the letters in the ciphertext (in percentages) are as follows: P 13.33 H 5.83 F 3.33 B 1.67 C 0.00 Z 11.67 D 5.00 W 3.33 G 1.67 K 0.00 S 8.33 E 5.00 Q 2.50 Y 1.67 L 0.00 U 8.33 V 4.17 T 2.50 I 0.83 N 0.00 O 7.50 X 4.17 A 1.67 J 0.83 R 0.00 M 6.67 Comparing this breakdown with Figure 3.5, it seems likely that cipher letters P and Z are the equivalents of plain letters e and t, but it is not certain which is which. The letters S, U, O, M, and H are all of relatively high frequency and probably correspond to plain letters from the set {a, h, i, n, o, r, s}. The letters with the lowest frequencies (namely, A, B, G, Y, I, J) are likely included in the set {b, j, k, q, v, x, z}. There are a number of ways to proceed at this point. We could make some tentative assignments and start to fill in the plaintext to see if it looks like a reasonable “skeleton” of a message. A more systematic approach is to look for other regularities. For example, certain words may be known to be in the text. Or we could look for repeating sequences of cipher letters and try to deduce their plaintext equivalents.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Figure 3.5 Relative Frequency of Letters in English Text

    الشكل يبيّن كم مرة يظهر كل حرف في النص الإنجليزي العادي.

    The figure shows how often each letter appears in ordinary English text.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

كيف تقرأ هذا المخطط؟ كل عمود = حرف، وارتفاعه = نسبة ظهوره من كل 100 حرف. مثلًا E = 12.702% يعني أن حوالي 13 حرفًا من كل 100 هي E.

لماذا يهمنا؟ الشيفرة أحادية الأبجدية تستبدل E دائمًا بنفس الحرف. فإذا كان أكثر حرف تكرارًا في النص المشفر هو مثلًا P، فغالبًا P = e. هكذا تنكسر رغم مفاتيحها الـ 26!.

How to read it: each bar is a letter; its height is how often it appears per 100 letters. E = 12.702% means about 13 of every 100 letters are E.

Why it matters: a monoalphabetic cipher always replaces E with the same letter. If the most common ciphertext letter is, say, P, then probably P = e. That is how it breaks despite its 26! keys.

الخلاصة

الحروف لها تكرارات ثابتة تقريبًا (E الأعلى)، وهذا يكشف الشيفرات أحادية الأبجدية.
Letter frequencies are fairly stable (E highest), which exposes monoalphabetic ciphers.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

A powerful tool is to look at the frequency of two-letter combinations, known as digrams . A table similar to Figure 3.5 could be drawn up showing the relative frequency of digrams. The most common such digram is th. In our ciphertext, the most common digram is ZW, which appears three times. So we make the correspondence of Z with t and W with h. Then, by our earlier hypothesis, we can equate P with e. Now notice that the sequence ZWP appears in the ciphertext, and we can translate that sequence as “the.” This is the most frequent trigram (three-letter combination) in English, which seems to indicate that we are on the right track. Next, notice the sequence ZWSZ in the first line. We do not know that these four letters form a complete word, but if they do, it is of the form th_t. If so, S equates with a. So far, then, we have UZQSOVUOHXMOPVGPOZPEVSGZWSZOPFPESXUDBMETSXAIZ t a e e te a that e e a a VUEPHZHMDZSHZOWSFPAPPDTSVPQUZWYMXUZUHSX e t ta t ha e ee a e th t a EPYEPOPDZSZUFPOMBZWPFUPZHMDJUDTMOHMQ e e e tat e the t Only four letters have been identified, but already we have quite a bit of the message. Continued analysis of frequencies plus trial and error should easily yield a solution from this point. The complete plaintext, with spaces added between words, follows: it was disclosed yesterday that several informal but direct contacts have been made with political representatives of the Viet cong in Moscow Monoalphabetic ciphers are easy to break because they reflect the frequency data of the original alphabet. A countermeasure is to provide multiple substitutes, known as homophones, for a single letter. For example, the letter e could be assigned a number of different cipher symbols, such as 16, 74, 35, and 21, with each homophone assigned to a letter in rotation or randomly. If the number of symbols assigned to each letter is proportional to the relative frequency of that letter, then single-letter frequency information is completely obliterated. The great mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss believed that he had devised an unbreakable cipher using homophones. However, even with homophones, each element of plaintext affects only one element of ciphertext, and multiple-letter patterns (e.g., digram frequencies) still survive in the ciphertext, making cryptanalysis relatively straightforward. Two principal methods are used in substitution ciphers to lessen the extent to which the structure of the plaintext survives in the ciphertext: One approach is to encrypt multiple letters of plaintext, and the other is to use multiple cipher alphabets. We briefly examine each.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Easy to break because they reflect the frequency data of the original alphabet

    سهلة الكسر لأن تكرارات الحروف في النص الأصلي تنتقل كما هي إلى النص المشفر.

    Easy to break because the plaintext's letter frequencies carry over into the ciphertext.

  2. Countermeasure is to provide multiple substitutes (homophones) for a single letter

    الحل المضاد: إعطاء الحرف الواحد عدة بدائل (homophones)، فمثلًا e تُشفَّر أحيانًا بـ X وأحيانًا بـ Q، فتتوزع تكراراته.

    Countermeasure: give one letter several substitutes (homophones), e.g. e becomes X sometimes and Q other times, spreading its frequency.

  3. Digram — Two-letter combination — Most common is th

    ثنائي الحروف (digram): تركيبة من حرفين، وأشهرها في الإنجليزية th.

    Digram: a two-letter combination; the most common is th.

  4. Trigram — Three-letter combination — Most frequent is the

    ثلاثي الحروف (trigram): تركيبة من ثلاثة، وأشهرها the.

    Trigram: a three-letter combination; the most frequent is the.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

حتى مع البدائل المتعددة، تبقى أنماط الحروف المتجاورة (th، the) ظاهرة في النص المشفر، فتساعد المهاجم. لهذا تأتي الشيفرات التالية: بلايفير (تشفّر حرفين معًا) وفيجنير (تغيّر الأبجدية عبر الرسالة) لإخفاء هذه الأنماط.

Even with homophones, patterns of neighbouring letters (th, the) still show in the ciphertext and help the attacker. That motivates the next ciphers: Playfair (encrypts two letters together) and Vigenère (changes the alphabet along the message) to hide these patterns.

الخلاصة

تحليل التكرار (حروف، ثنائيات، ثلاثيات) يكسر أحادية الأبجدية.
Frequency analysis (letters, digrams, trigrams) breaks monoalphabetic ciphers.

الشريحة 21 — Playfair Cipher

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Best-known multiple-letter encryption cipher
  • Treats digrams in the plaintext as single units and translates these units into ciphertext digrams
  • Based on the use of a 5 x 5 matrix of letters constructed using a keyword
  • Invented by British scientist Sir Charles Wheatstone in 1854
  • Used as the standard field system by the British Army in World War I and the U.S. Army and other Allied forces during World War II
